rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Biodiversity is the variety of life at three levels — genetic, species, and ecosystem. Conservation biology protects it through in-situ strategies (protected areas, community forests, sacred groves) and ex-situ strategies (zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks). Threats include habitat loss, overexploitation, pollution, invasive species, climate change, and poaching.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Biodiversity = genetic + species + ecosystem diversity
In-situ: protected areas + community forests + sacred groves (in natural habitat)
Ex-situ: zoos + botanical gardens + seed banks + gene banks + cryopreservation (outside habitat)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Biodiversity has THREE levels: genetic, species, ecosystem (not just "number of species").  ·  In-situ conservation protects species IN their natural habitat; ex-situ conserves them OUTSIDE (zoos, seed banks).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: NEB expects the three levels of biodiversity (genetic, species, ecosystem) with examples.  ·  In-situ vs ex-situ conservation: a very common comparison question.

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Genetic diversity: different rice varieties in Terai and hills; different rhododendron species.  ·  Species diversity: Chitwan (Bengal tiger, one-horned rhino), Annapurna (Himalayan flora).

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Protected areas (in-situ) are the most effective large-scale conservation strategy.  ·  Community forestry (in-situ) gives local communities rights and responsibility; it is Nepal's success story.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Biodiversity: genetic, species, ecosystem diversity.  ·  Conservation: in-situ (natural habitat) + ex-situ (outside).  ·  In-situ: protected areas, community forests, sacred groves.  ·  Ex-situ: zoos, botanical gardens, seed banks, gene banks.

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: About 64% of Nepal's total area is under forest; ~40% is under some protection.  ·  Community forest groups (22,000+) manage ~36% of Nepal's forest land.

rows.label: Extra solved
rows.text: Ecosystem diversity: Terai grassland, riverine forest, temperate oak-rhododendron, alpine meadow, nival zone.  ·  In-situ: Chitwan National Park, community forests, sacred groves (deval-ghari).

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: Biodiversity: the variety of life at three levels — genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity.  ·  Genetic diversity: variation in genes within a species; important for adaptation and survival.  ·  Species diversity: number and abundance of species in an area; higher in tropics.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Importance of conservation  ·  Threats: habitat loss, overexploitation, pollution, invasive species, climate change, poaching.  ·  Nepal: Himalaya hotspot; 64% forest; community forestry (~36%).

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: Why conserve: food, medicine, ecology, aesthetics, ethics.  ·  A biodiversity HOTSPOT has high endemic species AND severe habitat loss (both criteria).  ·  Conservation is not just "protecting animals"; it includes genetic, species, and ecosystem diversity.
